messages:
maria: Heads up — getting P99 spikes (~2.2s) on /v1/chat.generate for model rwd-7b-q8-2026-03 after last runtime rollout. P95 up ~400ms. Multiple customer tickets. anyone on call? @devon

infra-bot: Deploy finished: runtime v2.15.0 -> v2.15.1 at 2026-03-17T14:02Z (release-id: r-20260317-151).

devon: I see the spike in the metrics. Correlates with kernel selector switching some shards to FlashAttention SDPA variant for long-seq requests. digging into traces now. :thinking:

ben: Do we have a quick repro? length, batch size?

maria: Repro steps I used: 1) send two concurrent chat.generate requests with sequence length ~2048, batch_size=1, role:system+user. 2) observed p95 ~600ms, p99 ~2.3s. Endpoint: prod-us-west-2 pool. Logs snippet below:

```
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] req=0xaaa kernel_choice=flashattn_sdpa compile_flags="-O3 -ffast-math -march=native" seq_len=2048 batch=1 p99=2.35s
[2026-03-17T14:05:12Z] gpu=dgx-1 device=0 kv_cache_hits=0
```

devon: That compile flag (-ffast-math) is the smoking gun for SDPA math reorder regressions on our microbenchmarks. The new auto-compile profile added it in the last build. Two immediate mitigations: 1) force kernel heuristic to prefer sdpa_fallback for long sequences, or 2) flip instance-level ENABLE_FLASHATTN=0 to use fallback kernels.

ben: We already have an env toggle per pool. Can we patch the affected pool quickly?

devon: Yes — plan: roll a canary that disables FLASHATTN for prod-us-west-2 pool (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and also add a selector guard: if seq_len > 1024 and batch_size <= 4 prefer sdpa_fallback. I'll open a hotfix PR and kick a canary.

infra-bot: Canary rollout initiated: disable FLASHATTN on pool prod-us-west-2 at 3332110076 (10%).

maria: I'll update CS + escalation channel, tell the impacted customers we're rolling a mitigation. Which customers are in that pool?

ben: ABC-Corp and two small customers — I'll DM ops to confirm.

devon: For diagnostics, if you need to check kernel decisions for a trace run: `rdctl trace show <trace_id> --fields kernel,seq_len,batch,latency` also look at `/var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log` on the node.

devon: PR: https://git.internal/runtime/commit/def456 (adds heuristic guard, reverts -ffast-math in compile profile). Will revert compile profile until we can validate microbenchmarks.

ben: After canary finishes, we should run a quick perf job across representative seq lengths to confirm p95/p99 back to baseline. I'll queue perf-run: longseq-regen-2048.

maria: CS updated. They asked for ETA — tell them ~30m for canary -> 1h for full rollout if stable.

devon: Agreed. I'll watch traces and set alert throttle to avoid noisy pages but keep P99 threshold at 1.8s for now. If we see regression persisting after rollback, we'll do immediate rollback of the runtime release.

maria: Thanks all. Please post final status in this thread so I can close tickets. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Canary progressed to 50% at 3332110476.

devon: Canary at 50% looks good — p99 dropped from 2.3s -> 0.9s for the sampled traces. continuing to 100%.

infra-bot: Canary completed: 100% at 3332110876.

ben: Perf job results (quick): longseq-2048 p99=0.95s p95=0.58s on prod-west. Looks back to baseline.

maria: Closing loop with CS and affected customers. Leaving follow-ups: (1) formal postmortem on compile flags change, (2) add automated microbenchmark gate for compile profiles, (3) consider a more conservative default for kernel heuristics.

devon: I'll open the postmortem draft and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml. commit/PR links in the doc.

maria: Great, thanks everyone.
